# roxy

A strict, programmable HTTP firewall: an egress proxy for untrusted workloads, or a gateway in front of the APIs your clients call.

- [Overview](/index): roxy is a strict, programmable HTTP firewall: an egress proxy for untrusted workloads, or a gateway in front of the APIs your clients call.
- [Quickstart](/quickstart): Watch generated traffic go through roxy with an auth gate, a per-user token quota and an inspect_sentinel sidecar, against a scripted model.
- [Sandbox containment](/guides/containment): Run roxy as the only way out of a sandbox: the workload points HTTPS_PROXY at roxy's proxy port, trusts roxy's CA, and the network gives it no other route.
- [HTTP gateway](/guides/gateway): Put roxy in front of the APIs your clients call: a load balancer terminates TLS, an http listener takes each request, and rules route it by host and inject the real key.
- [Run roxy](/guides/run)
- [Node mode](/guides/node-mode)
- [Operations](/guides/operations)
- [Managing the CA](/guides/ca-certificates)
- [Testing a policy](/guides/testing-a-policy)
- [Writing addons](/guides/writing-addons)
- [How roxy works](/design/how-it-works): One exchange through roxy: decrypt and parse, the addon stack, the rules, the connector, and the response back up the same path, with every stage and every exit written to the flow log.
- [Threat model and guarantees](/design/threat-model)
- [Policy evaluation](/design/policy-evaluation): How the rules decide an exchange: one admission decision on the request head, in-flight re-checks as bytes stream, deny wins, and how effects, tags and unavailable inputs behave.
- [Addon model](/design/addon-model): What an addon layer is, how the stack is shaped, the invariants every layer is held to, how the bytes and the host-service effects of one layer are ordered against another's, and what the modes mean.
